standard_prerequisites.name: Computation of derived tensor by property (P) modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the derived tensors - tensor_A^L N and - tensor_A^L N' with plain tensors on property-(P) modules, the starting point for the transformation and its quasi-isomorphism analysis.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of filtered colimits and the filtration of property-(P) modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact; Same chapter, construction of property (P)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the tensor with M be read through the filtered system of its filtration stages, whose split inclusions give the short exact sequences the induction runs on.

core_obligations: Transformation of functors (proof lines 5568-5579): for M with property (P), 1 tensor f : M tensor_A N to M tensor_A N' is a map of differential graded B-modules, functorial in M; since both derived tensors are computed by tensoring property-(P) objects (lemma-derived-bc), this assembles into the transformation of functors.

Reduction to filtration stages (proof lines 5581-5590): M tensor_A N is the filtered colimit of F_i(M) tensor_A N (and likewise for N'); filtered colimits are exact (algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact), so it suffices to show each F_n(M) tensor_A N to F_n(M) tensor_A N' is a quasi-isomorphism.

Induction on the filtration (proof lines 5591-5603): the inclusions F_n(M) to F_{n+1}(M) are split as graded A-modules, giving short exact sequences of differential graded B-modules on tensors (and the analogue for N'), and f induces a map between them; by induction from n = -1 it suffices to handle the graded pieces.
The graded pieces (proof lines 5604-5607): F_{n+1}(M)/F_n(M) is a direct sum of shifts of A, and for A[k] the map is just f tensored with the identity, a quasi-isomorphism by hypothesis.
proof_roadmap: Assemble the transformation from the property-(P) computation of derived tensor.
Pass to the filtration stages through exactness of filtered colimits.
Induct on the filtration using the split inclusions and the induced maps of short exact sequences.
Conclude on the graded pieces, which are sums of shifts of A, by the hypothesis on f.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves functoriality of derived tensor in the bimodule and that quasi-isomorphisms of bimodules induce isomorphisms of functors (statement lines 5558-5568). The proof (lines 5570-5607) is a genuine four-beat argument: the property-(P) assembly of the transformation, the reduction to filtration stages through exactness of filtered colimits, an induction on the filtration through the induced maps of short exact sequences coming from the split inclusions, and the final evaluation on the graded pieces as sums of shifts of A. H2: the induction structure is the content and no step is a bare citation.
